notes.title: I have some bad news...
notes.notes:
So, I've decided to indefinitely delay chapter 3. It's safe to consider this a formal cancellation, though I'm not keeping a potential revisitation of chapter 3 off the table if I choose to do that somewhere down the line. This is not a decision I wanted to make, but if you've been following my announcements, you may realize why this is happening. I have already spoken at nauseum about my desire to not work in the Clickteam Engine anymore, and I think that it's flaws may have caught up to me. In a previous post, I discussed how inexplicable issues stopped the cloak from working in the chapter 3 levels. Since then, multiple similar issues have arisen regarding old mechanics (that used to work) that inexplicably stopped working. I have thoroughly investigated each of these and they all seem to be examples of code that works in some levels, but not in others. At this point, I am convinced that it is a memory problem with the engine, as no other explanation even makes sense as none of these mechanics even changed. As a result, I have decided that I'd be best served to move on to a new project. I appreciate all the support you have given to Xenoterrestrial over the years, and while this may not be goodbye forever, I wouldn't count on a return from me. It's been a long time coming for me to been done with both Xenoterrestrial and Clickteam, and I am excited to move on to new engines, new ideas, and new projects in the near future. Thanks again for all your support throughout the years!
-Cephalopod1112

notes.title: Chapter 3 Cut Content Situation Explained
notes.notes: Hello all. Unfortunately, I have had to recently make the decision to cut a significant piece of content from the upcoming chapter 3 update, meaning that the arsenal will be incomplete. As I've spoken about in the past, I've been itching to move on from this project and work on something different not because I've fallen out of love with Xenoterrestrial, but because I hate the game engine it is built in. In recent testing, an issue has arisen with the Cloak, a mechanic thus far only accessible in the sandbox. The cloak is designed to hide you from enemies for as long as you can go without dashing, taking damage, using the jackhammer, or shooting. Despite the seemingly obvious explanation that it sounds extremely unbalanced (though I'd actually assert that it's balanced due to the way level ranks work), there is a very different issue with the cloak that is preventing me from implementing it into the game. For some reason, in certain situations, only certain types of enemies seem to take an extended period of time to 'realize' that you are wearing the cloak and stop seeing you. The strange part is that the code that controls this is THE SAME for all enemies, but not all enemies have the problem. After checking REPEATEDLY and EXTENSIVELY, I cannot figure out for the life of me what is causing this issue. I even tried reprogramming the alertness mechanics of enemies from the ground up and the issue persisted. At this point, I am beginning to think that it's some kind of bizarre issue caused by the engine itself, as there is no logical explanation for why this would be happening. As a result, I have decided to delay the addition of the cloak indefinitely, though its codex entry, and the level and pedestal where it was intended to be given to the player will remain in the game. This is not a decision that I wanted to make, but the alternative was me seriously considering cancelling the update. Hopefully this isn't too much of a loss, I'm really not sure if I will ever revisit this (though I am leaving myself the option to). Otherwise, expect the rest of chapter 3 out this spring!

notes.notes: Hello all! I'd first like to announce that chapter 3 is officially coming this spring. As previously announced, chapter 3 will be the last major update to the game, after which I will move on to new projects in new engines. I have a lot of interesting ideas for what to do next, and those ideas are different then I may have originally stated, so I can't wait until that time comes. I've also made the decision to permanently reduce the price of the game to $2.99, as I feel it is a more appropriate price. Thanks for reading, I'm excited to get chapter 3 out to you all early this spring!

notes.title: Rampage Mode Announcement
notes.notes:
Hello all! I'd like to make a formal announcement regarding the upcoming release of rampage moed and the still-unannounced features coming in chapter 3. Note that some of the features originally intended for chapter 3 will be included as a part of this update because I figured it would be more fun and easier to program to include them as a part of rampage mode. They will be explained later in this post. 

First though, what is rampage mode? Rampage mode is the new arena-based endless mode experience for Xenoterrestrial. It is locked behind a level 10 requirement, but I promise it's a lot of fun (it's easily my favorite part of this game now). Every round, you are sent to a one of 8 different arenas, and a wave of enemies are spawned. The enemy spawns are related to which wave you're on, and the difficulty will ramp up over time. Between rounds, you are sent to a recovery room to resupply and are awarded skill points. This new system allows you to upgrade some of your stats and abilities as a player and can make a huge difference in the long run. One of my favorite things about this mode is that it has really revealed the uses of some of the lesser used weapon mods, enabling the use of far more interesting loadouts. There are even rewards for reaching certain waves. I'm very excited for you to try this new mode!
[i]
[b]Rampage mode will be releasing October 27, 2024![/b][/i]

But what about those new chapter 3 features? While not every chapter 3 feature will appear in rampage mode, all of the new enemies and some of the new level mechanics will, so here is a review of what to expect! Just know...I'm not going to reveal any of the stuff that won't be in this update just yet to keep some element of surprise.

[u][i]Enemies[/i][/u]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44680874/5fd94ce7e168b610113174e93189ffd1c7208457.png[/img]
[b]Stray[/b]
The stray is a unique enemy in that they don't directly target the player. They'll roam semi-randomly placing mines in a certain area. These mines will explode on contact and can't be destroyed on a whim, though they will dissapear on their own after a while. Notably, these mines do not emit a glow effect, which means they will become invisble if the screen is darkened, which is another new mechanic!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44680874/d3c1b13a748c3557293160c2bc417d09dc9ea02c.png[/img]
[b]Shade[/b]
The shade is a powerful mid-size enemy that will continuously darken your vision the longer it is on screen. it also shoots out an array of attacks that can be tricky to dodge and has access to blue defensive projectiles when it gets below half-health.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44680874/dc8c7924218f7be6a5038554f6fd87df4f198c2e.png[/img]
[b]Cleric[/b]
Another somewhat unique enemy, the Cleric does attack the player however it can't do damage. The cleric uses a combination of darkness projectiles, which significantly darken the screen on contact with the player, and healing projectiles, which target other enemies and can heal them even above their base health. These healing projectiles are actually parryable, and while a parry of one of these is very difficult to pull off, it is extremely rewarding.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44680874/f08dedeb0a994592b3446510acfabe254182e358.png[/img]
[b]Bastion[/b]
The bastion is another unique enemy which has a shield that orbits it, constantly facing the player. Virtually no attacks can go through the shield, but parried projectiles and the jackhammer can permanently disable it. The bastion also shoots a combination of rockets, magnets, and new repulsor bolts which knock you back and deal low damage. They are the most dangerous enemies in terms of area denial in the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44680874/0bf3fd9360ad27549df34d11030814dc1cdc00ae.png[/img]
[b]Eliminator[/b]
This enemy, which wears its inspirations on its sleeve, is designed to wear out the players stamina. They shoot high speed flechettes which are nearly impossible to dodge on higher difficulties and stick into surfaces (including the player) before exploding. These flechettes can be shaken off by dashing. They also can chase the player, fire parryable projectiles, and use sweep lasers. These guys are serious threats and should be treated as a top priority.

[i][u]Level Objects[/u][/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44680874/7feb42d84d4d12ba5219376698ec6522092853a3.png[/img]
[b]Black Hole[/b]
These portable black holes darken your vision the longer they're on screen. They can be temporarily disabled by the jackhammer.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44680874/ad7d2b2a68dca1a3152c778be98ff552ca33ab05.png[/img]
[b]Sentry[/b]
These Xyronian sentries continuously attack the player with sweep lasers and parryable projectiles, and cannot be destroyed using conventional methods. They can however be temporarily disabled by the jackhammer. Either way, your best bet is to limit line of sight with them as much as possible.

That's all I'll reveal for now... I'm excited for the release of this update next sunday. I hope you enjoy it!

notes.title: Xenoterrestrial Chapter 2 Formal Announcement and Teaser
notes.notes:
In this announcement, I'd like to tease/announce some of the new content that's coming soon to Xenoterrestrial. Note that much of what is discussed here is ALREADY COMPLETED and just currently inaccessible within the game.

[h2][b]NEW LEVELS AND CHAPTER[/b][/h2]
This new chapter, like the previous one, will include 8 new levels (with the 8th being a boss) and one new secret level. At present, only one of these levels is completely configured, but this is one of the only things in this announcement to not already be complete!

[h2][b]NEW MUSIC[/b][/h2]
Chapter 2 will contain new music for the main course of levels and a new boss theme from a [i]GUEST COMPOSER![/i] I am very excited to show off the new music when the time comes.

[h2][b]NEW ENEMIES[/b][/h2]
Chapter 2 will also contain 5 new enemy types, each of which I'll give a little tease of here. There is also a new boss, but I'm gonna keep that a secret for now.
The new enemies include:
[list]
[*][b]Commander:[/b] A new stronger variant of the soldier 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44680874/37020cf196f378ad561772341d43edc2cacd26cb.png[/img]
[*][b]Phantom:[/b] A weeping angel like enemy 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44680874/aa3163b2b787b1a993d51af3370eae31531a9806.png[/img]
[*][b]Biodrone:[/b] A new type of lighter enemy firing new parryable projectiles 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44680874/e91371da5c7d56c54935e960ba9a19ced1120317.png[/img]
[*][b]Bruiser:[/b] A beefy new enemy with a rocket launcher and meele attacks 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44680874/e0d0ef097a64aabf1762539492ca3c5abd46fc67.png[/img]
[*][b]Kilnhead:[/b] A towering beast equipped with a devastating flamethrower 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44680874/58703da7af0e02314c3336841d8ae987268baf02.png[/img]
[/list]

[h2][b]NEW WEAPONS AND GEAR[/b][/h2]
The new chapter will contain some new weapons and gear. While these have always been available in the sandbox, they will now be unlockable in the main course of the levels! Note that there are fewer new things than in chapter one as I am trying to space them out a bit more.
New items include:
[list]
[*] The Sniper Rifle: A heavy, long-range rifle with some interesting caveats.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44680874/bd956b378166b424e04c3a58a7840fd981d574f4.png[/img]
[*] The Jackhammer: This piece of gear is used to push back enemies and temporarily delay their attacks.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44680874/9d1f89334196acee1eaa5b571abfe950f1875c25.png[/img]
[*] The Grenade Launcher: Launches explosive grenades that can bounce off walls and deal heavy splash damage.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44680874/a63eeebc6cf6d61a4cb98f71294e60efc8a03e83.png[/img]
[/list]

[h2][b]NEW LEVEL MECHANICS[/b][/h2]
There are a number of new level mechanics in chapter 2. I won't show pictures of these because some of them are hard to show outside of screenshots, but I will offer a description.
[list]
[*] [h3][u]Updated Grapple Mechanics[/u][/h3]
         The grapple has been updated with a number of improvements and new interactions including:
         [list]
         [*] Improved clipping avoidance and fixes.
         [*] Added [i]Hookpoints[/i], a new level object that allows the player to hook to a point with no 
         collisions while automatically recharging their grapple.
         [*] Added [i]Kinetic Hookpoints[/i], which are the same as hookpoints but catapult you through 
         them on contact
         [*] Added [i]Pitfalls[/i], which can only be crossed using the grapple or rocket ride. These have a 
         lot of interesting interactions with Hookpoints.
         [/list]
[*] [b]Knockback Mechanics[/b] which can launch the player in uncontrollable ways.
[*] [b]Enemy Portals[/b] which continuously spawn enemies in certain areas.
[*] [b]Teleporter[/b] level objects that require the player to hold down the interact button to charge up a one-way teleport.
[/list]

[h2][b]RELEASE EXPECTATIONS[/b][/h2]
While I am not 100% confident, I would hazard to say to expect a May 2024 release for chapter 2. No promises though! I will work hard on this chapter to make sure that it is of a high quality and is more refined and complex than chapter one. Thank you for supporting Xenoterrestial, I am excited to work more on this game in the future.



And of course, there's another secret skin if you 100% complete the chapter (maybe even Xeno's first [i]youtuber crossover[/i]???).
